Test handles both timings.

minor.issue: After the exception path succeeds (state.facts.cutover.ok=true, cutover_exception recorded), state.awaiting stays 'cutover_check' rather than transitioning to 'decommission'. Root cause: Migrator.disable_missing_on_target() invokes self.cutover_check() synchronously (bypassing _bg), so the completion logic in _bg that sets awaiting=GATES[last]='decommission' never runs. Effect: an immediate POST /advance {step: 'decommission'} returns 409 'migration is not awaiting decommission (awaiting: cutover_check)'. Workaround: user must click CHECK CUTOVER once more, which chains through _bg and correctly transitions to awaiting='decommission'. Suggested fix: at the end of disable_missing_on_target, when cutover.ok is true and expected_accounts is now empty of missing, set state.awaiting='decommission' + state.current_step='cutover_check' explicitly, matching what _bg would do.

rca_of_the_issue: Minor bug: disable_missing_on_target() invokes cutover_check() synchronously in-process instead of through the _bg thread orchestration. The _bg completion block is the ONLY place state.awaiting is transitioned according to GATES; therefore a synchronous invocation of cutover_check() leaves awaiting untouched. Two possible fixes: (a) call _bg(None, 'cutover_check') from disable_missing_on_target so the standard completion path runs; (b) set state.awaiting='decommission' explicitly inside disable_missing_on_target when the resulting cutover.ok is True. Option (b) is safer (no thread races) and matches the semantics of the direct call. Reproduction: run advance freeze → let SIM-2 window drop → advance cutover_check (fails) → disable-missing (200) → immediate advance decommission returns 409. Mitigation currently required at test/UI level: run advance cutover_check one extra time.
